keyFindings.description: The restated test loses the location condition in the one paragraph that is about an extraction under $HOME, so the page sanctions at :47 what it refuses at :156. The paragraph opens on exactly that case — ':41 So that writable $HOME, and the issue's disk, are where an install for yourself would go', ':42-44 redis-cli, sqlite3 and dig did run from an extraction prefix under $HOME' — then rules: ':45-47 What rules such an attempt out is not the filesystem and not the unpacking: it is what the prefix leaves resolving ... and the test is scope. A prefix you export for the commands of your own run is sanctioned', closing at ':53-54 the room on the issue's disk does not touch it either'. The section that defines the test decides the same case the other way: ':119-123' makes condition 1 that what is written lands under the issue's own volume through a variable the runtime sets, and ':155-157' says 'an install under $HOME fails the first condition and is outside the sanctioned form, however little else it changes'. That section's own restatement of the scope test is correctly guarded — ':159-160 Between two installs that both land in the right place, the test is resolution, not disk' — and the copy at :47 lost the guard. So a role that asks the page's entry question, may I unpack a client under $HOME and export the prefix just around my own harness commands, is told yes at :47 and no at :156, and the placement :47 blesses is the one roleEnvironment exists to prevent after GKE Autopilot evicted issue pods for it (:152-155), for an extraction the options table measures at 105 MiB. The worked case itself is right ('into one root on the issue's volume', :173), which is what makes this a slip rather than a decision. One clause at :47 and :53-54 — borrow the guard the section below already has — and docs/kubernetes.md:176-187 carries the same unqualified sentence with no such section beside it.

The published operator page still carries the blanket mechanism ban this round removed everywhere else: 'apt cannot write a system prefix in an unprivileged container, unpacking one by hand works for some tools and not others, and Legion rules that route out as the withheld operator-setup capability'. That route is unpacking by hand, and Legion does not rule it out at this head: tools.md:47-49 states the rule as scope, tools.md:170-189 makes a hand-unpacked dpkg-deb -x root the worked sanctioned case, and four status: active learnings prescribe it, each annotated this round with 'still the step'. This round corrected the identical sentence in docs/kubernetes.md — the diff reads '-Legion rules that route out as the withheld operator-setup capability' / '+a client a role unpacks onto its own PATH is the withheld operator-setup capability' at :160 — and did not carry it here. It is the third hand-kept copy of one proposition, corrected in two. `grep -rn 'route out as the withheld' docs skills packages/claude-envoy AGENTS.md` returns exactly this one hit; my own sweep this round grepped three phrasings of the ban and this is a fourth, so the miss is on both of us and is itself the argument. One sentence, mirroring docs/kubernetes.md:159-161.

Both figures the architect ruled dropped are gone: no 'about 20 KB', no '2.5 GiB used', no '5.2 GiB used' anywhere in docs or skills.

The two grep commands run as printed find every site a new tool's name must reach, including worker.Dockerfile:417 (a redis-tools hit) and capabilitiestest.go (a redis-cli hit), plus all four Go files, AGENTS.md, docs/kubernetes.md and running-legion.md.
The committed bundle is byte-identical to skills/ (diff -r clean).
tools.md:155-157 and :159-160 say what finding 1 quotes, and running-legion.md:189 is the single surviving hit for the fourth phrasing.
acceptedThisRound: The prohibition restated as scope rather than mechanism, with the Dispatch e2e stack as the worked case and the harness's handoff note as what crosses to the next role.
The five learning notes, each pointing at the rule rather than superseding the recipe, and LEGION-748's second reason written as the contrast that makes the rest legible.

The site list replaced by two grep commands with the four gated Go sites named, the two kinds of hit that need more than a substitution called out, and the notices warning marked as a fact about this build with dispatch://INFRA-255 named as what ends it.
AGENTS.md:125 back to a pointer, naming the resolution test rather than carrying a second copy of the list.
reported: The scope test is now stated five times inside tools.md (:46-52, :100-107, :160-164, :179-183, :394-396), three of them in one 132-line section, two sharing a verbatim run. Every statement is true, so it does not meet the bar — but it is the generator of finding 1: a proposition held in N hand-kept copies gets corrected in N-1. The page's own thesis, written at :356-357, is 'Do not work from a list of those sites. This page has carried one twice and it was wrong both times.' The same move applies to the test: state it once where the section defines it, and let the other places point at it.
